callsites.required_change: Remove the private per-query ResolverQuery, RESOLVER_ID and resolver endpoint snapshots. Route every TCP hostname, including numeric/internal ones, through an explicit shared ResolutionContext. Keep a direct Unix-only path with no DNS dependency; no private fallback when a shared context is absent.

Make shared resolution explicit in configured TCP constructors, retain a DNS drain lease in the owned Connection, preserve independently cached service TCP/live Unix inputs. Remove legacy resolver-store argument in favor of the shared broker selected cfg owner.

Configured STATISTICS host must accept the caller shared resolution and use public transport Connection/ConnectionAttempt so service teardown cancels only its original DNS lease. Unix convenience can remain Unix-only without a private resolver.

Replace the standalone Resolver host default with the shared broker Context/Driver split. Preserve audited native_profile/check_config/native hostname utilities in a narrow IPC profile module to avoid a broker<->IPC dependency cycle. Do not retain the old query-private resolver driver as the official default.

Carry one SharedResolution from the process caller across all new ARM/monitor MQs; attach it to each endpoint. A cfg replacement changes selection only through the broker port, not by duplicating per-service resolver config.

Require/retain shared resolution on configured ARM constructors and every MQ rebuild. Preserve active attempt/stream/partial TX/RX and operation/callback ownership. Do not bind a fresh broker per control operation.
Use the same process SharedResolution as ClientHost for monitor TCP attempts and reconnects, retaining each successful service socket DNS drain lease until actual END or Drop.

Create or receive exactly one caller-owned broker context/driver for the process domain; pass the same shared resolution to control and monitor, and drive it concurrently with PROGRAM logical clock and both host owners. Teardown respects Query/Connection/Driver ownership; no private per-query MQ.
This public one-shot helper is explicitly Unix-only. It needs no resolver context and must stay Unix-only rather than gain a hidden resolver connection.

PROGRAM.port: Program ResolverConnect uses Context::connect(cfg.duplicate()?) at fixed native pre-main callsites; one SharedClock Subscription implements RuntimeClock. The same broker/driver must be supplied through process context to all service clients.
